stem.text: An open-top storage bin is made from a square sheet of steel 42 decimeters on a side by cutting a square of side x from each corner and folding up the sides. Find the largest possible volume of the storage bin, in cubic decimeters.

worked_solution.text: The storage bin has height x and a square base of side \( 42 - 2 x \), so its volume is \( V(x) = x\left(42 - 2 x\right)^{2} \).
The cut must be positive and less than half the sheet, so the domain is \( 0 < x < 21 \).
\( V'(x) = 12 \left(x - 21\right) \left(x - 7\right) \), which is zero at \( x = 7 \) and \( x = 21 \); only \( x = 7 \) lies strictly inside the sheet.
\( V'(x) \) is positive for \( 0 < x < 7 \) and negative for \( 7 < x < 21 \), and this is the only critical point in the domain, so V has its absolute maximum there.
worked_solution.rule_named: first derivative test for an absolute extremum

worked_solution.text: The largest volume is \( V(7) = 7\left(28\right)^{2} = 5488 \) cubic decimeters.

options.derivation: the critical point x = 21 from the factor of the base taken without checking what kind of point it is, giving the volume there
the side of the cut square, where the maximum occurs, reported instead of the volume
the side of the base at the optimum reported instead of the volume
